Ligand 1 is the aryl urea at jnk3 0.06 again, ligand 2 a fluoro ester - no crossover worth making. Atom 0 is a dimethylamino methyl over an acyclic bond. Every cap I have tested is a saturated carbocycle, and all of them - cyclopropyl, cyclobutyl, cyclopentyl, oxetanyl - score identically, which told me ring size is irrelevant but not whether the cap could do real work. This episode gives it a ring that can. A picolinamide cap puts a pyridine on the carbonyl with its ring nitrogen ortho to the carbonyl, so the molecule now presents two ortho-nitrogen azines instead of one: the established one on the arylamine, and a second at the far end. That is a direct test of whether the feature that earns activity is additive when placed somewhere genuinely different, as opposed to the bis-arylamine I tried before, which simply duplicated the same linkage and cost more QED than it gained. The cost here is about 3 Da over the cyclobutyl cap plus a third aromatic ring, so QED will fall to roughly 0.80 - meaning this only wins if jnk3 moves well past 0.52. Surviving methyl becomes the pyridine 4-methyl.
